headings.title: Prohibition on local rent control ordinances
headings.reviewNote: Covers state statutory prohibition barring counties and cities from enacting or enforcing rent control ordinances on private rental property.

headings.title: Prohibitions on local restrictions regarding screening and leasing criteria
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibitions on local ordinances restricting landlord discretion regarding housing assistance vouchers, credit criteria, deposits, or refusal rights.

headings.title: Exceptions for municipally owned property and subsidized housing agreements
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory exceptions allowing municipal regulation of public property, voluntary rent agreements, and block grant housing restrictions.

headings.title: Local ordinances prohibiting discrimination based on veterans' benefits
headings.reviewNote: Covers authorization for local ordinances prohibiting landlords from discriminating against tenants based on receipt of veterans' benefits.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text (A.L. 2025 H.B. 595 & 343): preemption of local rent control and screening/deposit/first-refusal restrictions, exceptions for public property and subsidized/CDBG housing, and preservation of veterans'-benefits anti-discrimination ordinances.

headings.title: Termination of tenancies at will, sufferance, or under one year
headings.reviewNote: Covers termination of tenancies at will, by sufferance, or for less than one year by one month's written notice.

headings.title: Presumption of reasonableness for two persons per bedroom occupancy limit
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory presumption that occupancy limitation of two persons per bedroom is reasonable, excluding newborn children.

headings.title: Unwritten nonagricultural building tenancies deemed month to month
headings.reviewNote: Deems unwritten agreements for buildings in cities, towns, or villages and other nonagricultural buildings (except garden purposes) to be month-to-month tenancies terminable by either party on one month's written notice.

headings.title: Termination of month-to-month tenancies and sixty-day mobile home lot notice
headings.reviewNote: Covers written notice requirements for terminating month-to-month tenancies and sixty-day notice mandate for owned mobile homes on leased lots.

headings.title: Self-help possession by landlord in presence of law enforcement officer
headings.reviewNote: Covers procedure for landlord possession and property removal in officer's presence if service officer fails to deliver execution within seven days.

headings.title: Landlord immunity from liability for removed personal property
headings.reviewNote: Shields landlords from liability for loss or damage to personal property removed under subsection 5, except for negligent, willful, or wanton acts or omissions or failure to timely obtain and file the officer acknowledgment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text (including cross-reference to section 432.050 and 1956/1962/1963 case annotations); broadened subsection 3 title to cover nonagricultural buildings generally and corrected subsection 6 reviewNote to include negligence and acknowledgment-filing exceptions.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of oral evidence to prove renewal of written lease
headings.reviewNote: Covers inadmissibility of oral evidence to prove extension or renewal of written lease in holdover possession suits, requiring written contract.

headings.title: Inadmissibility of oral testimony to alter termination notice in oral letting
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that variation or abrogation of termination notice in oral or agricultural tenancies be established by dated written evidence.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text (including cross-reference to section 534.290 and 1953 Harriman case annotation): inadmissibility of oral evidence to prove written lease renewal or alter oral-tenancy termination notices.

headings.title: Unlawful exclusion of tenant or property deemed forcible entry and detainer
headings.reviewNote: Covers classification of extrajudicial lockout or removal of tenant or property by landlord as forcible entry and detainer under chapter 534.

headings.title: Willful interruption of essential utility services deemed forcible entry
headings.reviewNote: Covers classification of willful utility shutoffs as forcible entry and detainer, except when interrupted for health or safety reasons.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: landlord unlawful exclusion/lockout (except under section 441.065) and willful utility interruption (absent health/safety reasons) deemed chapter 534 forcible entry and detainer.

headings.title: Tenant qualifications for repair and deduct remedy
headings.reviewNote: Covers eligibility criteria requiring six months of consecutive lawful residence, rent paid, and cure of any lease violations.

headings.title: Repair and deduct procedure, cost limits, and municipal code certification
headings.reviewNote: Allows repair-and-deduct after 14 days' written notice (or promptly in emergencies) for code-violating habitability, sanitation, or security conditions costing under the greater of $300 or half periodic rent (capped at one month's rent), with municipal certification if disputed, non-exclusive remedies, and no lease waiver.

headings.title: Exclusion of tenant-caused conditions and annual deduction cap
headings.reviewNote: Covers exclusion of repairs caused by tenant fault and annual cap limiting aggregate deductions to one month's rent in twelve months.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 3 subsections against archived text; corrected subsection 2 reviewNote to state the exact repair cost limit (greater of $300 or half periodic rent, capped at one month's rent), non-exclusivity, and waiver prohibition.

headings.title: Grounds for landlord attachment of property and crops for unpaid rent
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory grounds for rent attachment including property removal, crop disposal endangering collection, and unpaid rent after demand.

headings.title: Attachment affidavit, double indemnity bond, and purchaser crop liability
headings.reviewNote: Covers attachment issuance upon affidavit, plaintiff bond in double amount sued, and purchaser liability for buying crops with knowledge.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text (including chapter 521 cross-reference and 1993 Jenkins crop-lien case annotation): six rent-attachment grounds, affidavit and double-bond procedure, and knowledgeable crop-purchaser liability.

headings.title: Petition for court-appointed receiver to abate housing code violations
headings.reviewNote: Covers application by county, municipality, housing corporation, or neighborhood association for receiver to abate code violations threatening safety.

headings.title: Sixty-day written notice of intent to apply for receivership
headings.reviewNote: Covers sixty-day advance notice requirement to interested parties identifying property, code violations, contact office, and potential receivership.

headings.title: Prohibition on receivership application during pending foreclosure or contract suit
headings.reviewNote: Covers bar on applying for receivership if an interested party is actively prosecuting foreclosure, specific performance, or forfeiture proceedings.

headings.title: Service of receivership application on all interested parties
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory service of the receivership application upon all interested parties.

headings.title: Correction of conditions by interested party upon posting court security
headings.reviewNote: Covers election by interested parties to correct conditions and requirement to post security to ensure timely performance of repairs.

headings.title: Judicial determination of unsafe condition and appointment of receiver
headings.reviewNote: Covers court finding of unsafe or insanitary condition and appointment of receiver when interested parties fail to act or perform corrections.

headings.title: Receiver exempt from bond requirement prior to appointment
headings.reviewNote: Covers exemption providing that court-appointed receivers are not required to post security or bond prior to appointment.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text: code-violation receivership petitions, 60-day notice, pending foreclosure/contract-suit bar, service, interested-party correction with security, unsafe-condition finding, and pre-appointment bond exemption.

headings.title: Commencement of receivership action by verified petition
headings.reviewNote: Covers commencement of receivership action by verified petition filed by county, municipality, housing corporation, or neighborhood association.

headings.title: Mandatory party defendants in receivership action
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement to name the last owner of record and last mortgage or lienholder of record as party defendants.

headings.title: Joinder of nonparty owners as defendants
headings.reviewNote: Covers judicial permission for nonparty owners of the dwelling to join the action as defendants.

headings.title: Jurisdiction, personal service, and nonresident agent designation
headings.reviewNote: Covers personal jurisdiction, service of process, and mandatory designation of resident agent for service with secretary of state.

headings.title: Expedited judicial proceedings and case precedence
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that courts expedite receivership actions and authorization to give them precedence over other civil suits.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 5 subsections against archived text: verified petition commencement, mandatory defendants, permissive owner joinder, personal jurisdiction and nonresident/corporate agent designation, and expedited proceedings.

headings.title: Court orders authorizing rent expenditures and appointing receivers
headings.reviewNote: Covers judicial orders authorizing rent draws for repairs and appointing qualified receivers subject to lienholder right of first refusal.

headings.title: Allowance of reasonable and necessary receiver expenses
headings.reviewNote: Covers court authorization to allow receiver reasonable and necessary expenses payable from deposited rent funds.

headings.title: Mandatory court-approved receiver bond
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that appointed receivers provide court-approved bond paid from deposited rent moneys.

headings.title: Receiver authority to take possession, collect rents, and pay taxes
headings.reviewNote: Covers receiver authority under court order to possess property, collect rents and profits, and pay management expenses, insurance, and taxes.

headings.title: Duty to remove violations and contracting authority
headings.reviewNote: Covers receiver duty to expeditiously remove code violations constituting nuisances and power to let repair contracts under local laws.

headings.title: Borrowing authority, encumbrances, and issuance of receiver certificates
headings.reviewNote: Covers court-approved receiver borrowing, encumbering property, and issuing receiver certificates constituting superior first liens.

headings.title: Pledge of rental income as borrowing security
headings.reviewNote: Covers receiver power to pledge property rentals and borrow funds on the security of rental income.

headings.title: Receiver lien on rents receivable and statutory priority
headings.reviewNote: Covers receiver lien upon rents receivable for necessary expenses, having priority over other liens except taxes and pre-1969 mortgages.

headings.title: Local housing corporation temporal restriction
headings.reviewNote: Covers restriction defining local housing corporations as only those established prior to August 28, 2001.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 9 subsections against archived text: section 441.570 court orders and receiver right of first refusal, expenses, mandatory bond, possession/rent/tax powers, violation removal, borrowing and first-lien receiver certificates, rental pledges, rent-receivable lien priority, and pre-August 28, 2001 local housing corporation limit.

headings.title: Definitions for master-metered multitenant dwelling utility receivership
headings.reviewNote: Covers definitions for delinquency, electrical corporation, gas corporation, heat-related utility service, master-metered multitenant dwelling, and owner.

headings.title: Five-day posted notice to tenants prior to service termination
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that utility corporations notify tenants five days prior to termination by posting notices of delinquency and receivership rights.

headings.title: Petition for receiver of rents and expedited hearing procedure
headings.reviewNote: Permits utility or tenant petitions in associate circuit court for a rent receiver, with a 2-day show-cause order and 4-day hearing; source footnote notes referenced sections 515.240 to 515.260 were repealed in 2016.

headings.title: Prohibition against terminating heat-related service during receivership proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against utilities shutting off heat-related service while a petition is pending with notice or a receivership is in effect.

headings.title: Powers and duties of receiver and priority of fund disbursements
headings.reviewNote: Covers receiver powers, posting contact notices, rent collection, and five-tier disbursement priority for costs, utilities, attorney fees, and owner.

headings.title: Owner liability for reasonable costs incurred by receiver
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory liability of master-metered dwelling owners for all reasonable costs incurred by court-appointed receivers.

headings.title: Circumstances requiring termination of receivership and accounting
headings.reviewNote: Mandates receivership termination and a complete court accounting upon a 3-month proceeds shortfall, projected deficit, fewer than 75 percent of tenants paying rent for two consecutive periods, or full payment of amounts owed.

headings.title: Petition by utility or owner for termination or change of receiver
headings.reviewNote: Allows the utility or owner to petition to terminate the receivership or replace the receiver, with a 30-day hearing deadline and advance written notice; original-rolls footnote notes word "for".

headings.title: Contempt of court for owner rent collection during receivership
headings.reviewNote: Covers contempt of court penalty for owners who collect or attempt to collect rents from tenants during an active receivership.

headings.title: Utility rights to recover lawful debts preserved
headings.reviewNote: Covers reservation of gas and electrical corporation rights to recover amounts lawfully owed, subject only to service termination limits.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 10 subsections against archived text; noted 2016 repeal of sections 515.240–515.260 in subsection 3, fixed subsection 7 reviewNote (fewer than 75% paying rent, not 75% nonpaying), and noted original-rolls footnote ("for") in subsection 8.

headings.title: Associate circuit court jurisdiction, expedited hearing, and summons
headings.reviewNote: Covers filing expedited eviction actions in associate circuit court and mandatory hearing within fifteen days of summons service.

headings.title: Prohibition on continuances or stays absent extraordinary reasons
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory prohibition barring continuances or stays in expedited eviction actions except for compelling and extraordinary reasons.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: associate circuit court venue, summons, 15-day expedited hearing under sections 441.710 to 441.880, and bar on continuances or stays absent compelling and extraordinary reasons.

headings.title: Mandatory eviction grounds for emergencies, drugs, or barred persons
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate eviction or a section 441.830 order (subject to sections 441.750 and 441.880) for imminent injury or severe property damage exceeding 12 months' rent (including subsidies), drug-related criminal activity, or allowing/failing to report return of a barred person.

headings.title: Immediate removal and bar from property for criminal actors
headings.reviewNote: Requires immediate removal and immediate barring from leased property of any person engaging in section 441.740 criminal activity on or in the immediate vicinity of the premises, subject to section 441.880.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text (A.L. 2023 S.B. 106); expanded subsection 1 title to include barred-person grounds and removed unstated "permanently" qualifier from subsection 2 reviewNote.

headings.title: Affirmative defenses to eviction for non-involved or coerced tenants
headings.reviewNote: Covers affirmative defense precluding eviction where tenant did not assist, had no knowledge, or acted under verbal or physical coercion.

headings.title: Five-day notice requirement for third-party criminal activity
headings.reviewNote: Covers five-day written notice requirement to tenant before filing suit for third-party activity and protective or police action remedy.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: affirmative defenses for non-involved or coerced tenants and 5-day written notice with protective-order or law-enforcement reporting cure for third-party criminal activity.

headings.title: Immediate removal of criminal actor without tenancy termination
headings.reviewNote: Covers court order immediately removing offending individuals while preserving tenancy when tenant successfully proves affirmative defense.

headings.title: Immediate removal of unlawful occupants
headings.reviewNote: Covers mandatory court order directing immediate removal of persons occupying dwelling units without lawful status as tenant or lessee.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text; noted catchline-vs-body mismatch (catchline references removal of tenant or lessee while subsection 2 requires removal of persons not lawfully occupying as a tenant or lessee).

headings.title: Twenty-four-hour vacate order and landlord right of reentry
headings.reviewNote: Covers court eviction order requiring tenant to vacate within twenty-four hours and granting landlord right to reenter and possess premises.

headings.title: Order barring removed individuals without tenancy termination
headings.reviewNote: Covers removal and barring of persons engaging in criminal activity while preserving the tenant's leasehold rights.

headings.title: Expedited execution within specified days after final judgment
headings.reviewNote: Covers judicial discretion to order expedited execution of eviction or removal orders within a specified number of days.

headings.title: Stay of execution upon clear and convincing evidence of serious danger
headings.reviewNote: Covers stay of execution for reasonable time upon clear and convincing proof that immediate removal poses serious danger outweighing public safety.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 4 subsections against archived text: 24-hour vacate order and landlord reentry, third-party removal without terminating tenancy, permissive expedited execution, and permissive stay on clear and convincing proof of serious danger.

headings.title: Civil eviction action independent of criminal prosecution
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that civil eviction actions proceed regardless of whether criminal prosecutions have commenced, ended, or failed to convict.

headings.title: Collateral estoppel effect of criminal conviction
headings.reviewNote: Covers collateral estoppel barring convicted defendants from challenging essential criminal allegations in subsequent civil proceedings.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified both subsections against archived text: independence of civil eviction actions from criminal prosecution and collateral estoppel effect of drug-related criminal convictions.

headings.title: Mandatory stay of eviction upon qualifying findings
headings.reviewNote: Requires a stay of removal or eviction execution if the movant establishes all six statutory findings, including drug dependency with prompt entry into court-approved treatment or tenant non-involvement in drug activity, absence of school/minor drug sales and weapons, no section 441.820 protective order, no prior stay, and no community or plaintiff danger.

headings.title: Notice of stay application to plaintiff and interested parties
headings.reviewNote: Covers requirement that reasonable notice of stay application be provided to plaintiffs and interested requesting parties.

headings.title: Probationary tenancy duration, terms, and conditions
headings.reviewNote: Requires probationary tenancy for the shorter of six months or the lease duration, allowing court-imposed or modified conditions including periodic drug testing, community service, and drug treatment for drug-dependent defendants.

headings.title: Rescission of stay upon noncompliance and expedited hearing
headings.reviewNote: Covers motion alleging probation noncompliance, five-day written notice, expedited hearing, and immediate rescission of stay upon violation.

headings.title: Subsequent conduct eviction rights and nonrenewal preserved
headings.reviewNote: Covers preservation of rights to evict for subsequent conduct and landlord rights to refuse lease renewals under existing law.

headings.title: Discharge of eviction order and dismissal upon probation completion
headings.reviewNote: Covers motion for discharge upon substantial probation compliance and automatic discharge and dismissal upon expiration of term.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 6 subsections against archived text; revised subsection 1 title to cover both treatment and non-involvement paths and corrected subsection 3 title and reviewNote (periodic drug testing, not periodic reporting).

headings.title: Definitions for domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking
headings.reviewNote: Covers definitions for domestic violence, sexual assault, and stalking referencing chapter 455 definitions.

headings.title: Protection against lease denial or eviction for abuse victims
headings.reviewNote: Covers prohibition against denying tenancy, evicting, or penalizing abuse victims, with exceptions for invited perpetrators or safety threats.

headings.title: Affirmative defense against unpaid rent after vacating premises
headings.reviewNote: Covers affirmative defense shielding abuse victims from rent liability after vacating premises upon notice and documentation.

headings.title: Qualifying statements and documentation of abuse
headings.reviewNote: Covers qualification standards by victim statement and requested documentation from service providers, professionals, police, or courts.

headings.title: Sanctions for submission of false abuse information
headings.reviewNote: Covers rule that submitting false abuse information provides grounds for lease denial, eviction, or lease agreement violation.

headings.title: Reasonable early lease termination fees authorized
headings.reviewNote: Covers landlord authority to impose reasonable early termination fees on tenants terminating leases under victim protection rules.

headings.title: Applicability restricted to residential properties
headings.reviewNote: Covers statutory restriction limiting the provisions and protections of section 441.920 to residential rental properties.

entries.reviewSummary: Verified all 7 subsections against archived text (L. 2019 H.B. 243 & 544): section 455.010 definitions, abuse-victim anti-discrimination protections and exceptions, post-vacate rent defense, documentation, false-information sanctions, permissive termination fees, and residential-only scope.
